target_readiness: beginner-ready Azure AI / Microsoft Foundry programming

prerequisites.why_it_matters_for_azure: Python is the minimum entry point for any Foundry SDK sample or lightweight client app.

prerequisites.skill_name: Use the terminal for simple commands
prerequisites.why_it_matters_for_azure: Learners need a terminal to install packages, run scripts, and inspect output before Azure tooling feels approachable.
Printing values is the fastest way to verify prompt payloads, responses, and intermediate JSON fields.
Prompts, endpoints, deployment names, file paths, and JSON keys are all string-heavy in Azure AI work.
prerequisites.notes: Introduced in L-01-02 through quoted survey labels and variable-backed print output.

prerequisites.why_it_matters_for_azure: Configuration values, flags, and control flow all depend on simple numeric and boolean reasoning.
prerequisites.notes: Introduced in L-01-02 by contrasting numeric channel_count with quoted strings and identifying True/False as booleans.

prerequisites.why_it_matters_for_azure: SDK clients, prompts, keys, and response objects all need named variables to stay understandable.
prerequisites.notes: Introduced in L-01-02 through assignment, reassignment, prediction, and later variable use.

prerequisites.skill_name: Read tracebacks and fix simple errors
prerequisites.why_it_matters_for_azure: Beginners must survive syntax and runtime errors before they can work through SDK setup or API responses.
prerequisites.notes: Introduced in L-01-03 through a NameError traceback diagnosis, a misspelled-variable repair, and a fresh IndentationError repair with route-safe retry.

prerequisites.why_it_matters_for_azure: Batch prompts, message histories, and grouped results are list-shaped in AI client applications.
JSON objects map directly to Python dictionaries, which is essential for request and response payloads.
prerequisites.notes: RP-002 reinforces PY-009 after L-03-01 with one two-key dictionary update: preserve source, None identity, and False access state while adding only an unknown classification and human owner. Primary and blank fresh transfer require 6/6 plus a closed-note key/value and None-versus-False explanation; photorealistic Scene evidence is unscored.

prerequisites.why_it_matters_for_azure: Branching is needed to handle success, failure, missing keys, and simple workflow decisions.
prerequisites.notes: RP-003 reinforces only the learner-owned equality condition and corresponding/different branches over a supplied loop scaffold. Primary and genuinely blank transfer require 8/8, with answer-free remediation and a closed-note condition/branch/unavailable explanation; the sealed source remains unread and None rather than false.

prerequisites.why_it_matters_for_azure: Loops are useful for traversing extracted items, repeated prompts, and collections of analysis results.
prerequisites.notes: RP-004 reinforces PY-011 after L-03-02 with one loop over three sanitized replica dictionaries and exactly one ordered correspondence record per iteration. Primary and genuinely blank transfer require 8/8, answer-free remediation, and a delayed closed-note iterable/current-item/body/output-count/purpose-boundary trace; SC-05 presentation is unscored and no live source is read or controlled.

prerequisites.why_it_matters_for_azure: Functions create reusable units for prompt calls, parsing steps, and simple client app structure.
Foundry SDK usage starts with imports, and learners need the mental model before SDK examples feel readable.
SDK setup depends on package installation and a beginner-safe model of project environments.
Image, audio, document, and output handling all depend on local file basics before Content Understanding work.
Azure and Foundry requests and responses are structured as JSON, so learners need to inspect and shape nested data.
API keys and endpoints should be introduced safely before any client app or endpoint workflow.
Endpoints and SDK abstractions make more sense when learners know what a request, response, header, and payload are.
This bridges generic programming into the Foundry implementation domain without requiring backend depth.
Prompts, extraction results, and multimodal app workflows all require learners to move comfortably through structured data.
prerequisites.notes: RP-001 reinforces this skill after L-03-01 and L-06-03 with one unseen expedition-owned anchor-packet parse, nested update, JSON serialization, and round-trip probe before CUM-01. It introduces no new prerequisite and cannot change physical city state.
